narrative:
**Engagement rebounded sharply week over week but remains flat on a one-month view.** Model downloads reached 3,835,859 across 26,945 tracked models, up 45.4% from the prior week yet down 1.2% versus four weeks ago — consistent with a bounce off a weak comparison week rather than a new level. Model likes followed the same pattern at 12,054 (+51.4% w/w, −8.8% vs. 4w), while Spaces likes at 1,207 rose on both horizons (+34.9% w/w, +18.3% vs. 4w) off a base of 6,920 Spaces. On the model side, family mix shifted toward smaller challengers: DeepSeek roughly doubled to 309 models (from about 155) and NVIDIA Nemotron rose to 210 (from about 78), while Qwen fell 9.1% to 5,467 (from about 6,016) and Gemma fell 16.9% to 838 (from about 1,009). GLM/Zhipu (79, from about 139) and Kimi/Moonshot (37, from about 78) also declined, though at those counts the week-to-week swings are volatile.

**Spaces growth was broad-based and concentrated in assistant, data and search workloads.** Chat-assistant Spaces rose 12.6% to 1,075, data-analysis 15.9% to 548, search-research 13.7% to 423, and coding 6.6% to 226; image-generation was the main decliner, down 5.6% to 693. Robotics (58, from 49) and music-generation (58, from 60) moved but are too few to report meaningfully in percentage terms. By SDK, Docker grew fastest at +16.7% to 560, with Static up 5.9% to 3,937 and Gradio up 7.0% to 2,296; Streamlit fell to 61 from about 83 — again, too small a base to lean on. On capability tags, local-inference penetration rose to 3.15% of Spaces (+17.2% w/w, +24.8% vs. 4w) and MoE to 0.90% (+31.8% w/w), while vision-language (7.02%, −6.6%) and multimodal (5.20%, −9.7%) softened. Among verticals, media-entertainment (9.93%, +12.6%), industrial-manufacturing (3.66%, +14.4%) and finance (3.79%, +11.9%) gained; consumer (8.89%, −7.9%) and scientific-research (7.95%, −6.3%) slipped.

**Two methodology caveats matter for interpretation.** First, 10,123 of 26,945 models (37.6%) carry an unknown family label, so family-level shares and their deltas are sensitive to classification coverage rather than developer behavior alone. Second, several use-case family cuts rest on very small denominators — music-generation (23 Spaces), education (30), robotics (33) and 3D/gaming (50) — so large swings there, including the +247% move for GLM/Zhipu within chat-assistant (about 8 Spaces) and the +830% move for Nemotron within voice-audio (10 Spaces), are too few to report reliably. Spaces use-case counts were at full coverage (1.0), and no 12-week comparisons were available this week. Next week, watch whether the download and likes rebound holds above the four-week average or reverts, and whether DeepSeek and Nemotron model counts sustain their gains against Qwen's decline.
